tagline: The charter capital of the eastern Mediterranean — where the world's superyachts gather, but every guest transfer is still a slow diesel hop.
summary: Bodrum and the Turquoise Coast — Datça, Göcek, Marmaris, Fethiye — are the premium yachting and gulet heartland of Turkey, anchored by the D-Marin marina chain and a roster of the world's top hospitality brands (Mandarin Oriental, Six Senses Kaplankaya, Maxx Royal, Caresse, Macakizi). It is dense with high-yield guests crossing short, scenic water gaps between marinas, resorts and the Greek Dodecanese — yet every one of those hops is still made on a conventional tender, gulet or fast-ferry. Bodrum is Navier's primary commercial node in the factory market: the obvious home-turf flagship.

use_cases.title: Marina-to-marina superyacht & resort transfers
use_cases.body: D-Marin Yalıkavak/Turgutreis to Göcek, Datça and the resort jetties on the Pioneer II — replacing slow tenders and gulets with a smooth, silent, branded foiling 'Navier Experience' arrival for high-yield guests.

use_cases.title: Cross-border to the Greek Dodecanese
use_cases.body: Bodrum↔Kos (~10 nm) and Marmaris↔Rhodes (~30 nm) on the Pioneer II: an on-demand premium foiling crossing through established CIQ ports, replacing the fixed-schedule diesel fast-ferry.

use_cases.title: Turquoise Coast line-haul Bodrum↔Göcek/Fethiye
use_cases.body: The full coastal run from Bodrum east to Göcek and Fethiye (>70 nm by sea around the Datça and Marmaris peninsulas) on the Quanta-LR hybrid — one comfortable leg versus a long peninsular drive, with no charging dependency.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The dense marina-and-resort mesh — Yalıkavak↔Turgutreis↔Datça (~10–20 nm), Bodrum↔Kos (~10 nm), Marmaris↔Rhodes (~30 nm), Göcek↔Fethiye (~10 nm) — sits inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope, ideal for high-frequency premium rotations.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The long Turquoise Coast line-haul Bodrum↔Göcek/Fethiye (>70 nm around two peninsulas) is a Quanta-LR hybrid corridor; the hybrid removes any charging-infrastructure dependency along the undeveloped stretches and opens longer charter itineraries (H2 2026+).

competitive_landscape: The water here is busy but entirely conventional: gulets and tenders for charter and resort transfers, and diesel fast-ferries (Bodrum Ferryboat Association, Yeşil Marmaris Lines) on the Greek crossings. The yacht-charter and blue-cruise sector is dense and sophisticated — strong evidence of demand and willingness to pay — but offers no foiling, on-demand, or zero-emission premium tier. That undifferentiated status quo, on a coast defined by the quality of the experience, is precisely the opening.
seasonality: A long Aegean/Mediterranean season (Apr–Oct). The summer meltemi (etesian) NW wind builds afternoon chop across the open gulfs — exactly where foiling's smoother, faster ride beats a pounding planing tender or gulet. Winter (Nov–Mar) narrows service to settled windows.
regulatory_note: Turkey is Navier's factory market and Bodrum its primary commercial node, with home classification via Türk Loydu — a uniquely clean regulatory path for a domestic flagship. Cross-border hops to Kos and Rhodes run through established Turkish/Greek CIQ ferry ports. D-Marin operates Blue Flag clean-marina infrastructure that aligns naturally with an all-electric fleet, and premium hospitality partners have strong appetite to operate their own vessels.
signature_routes: D-Marin Yalıkavak ↔ Turgutreis ↔ Datça (all-electric marina mesh)
Bodrum ↔ Göcek / Fethiye — Turquoise Coast line-haul (Quanta-LR hybrid)

precedents.what: ~$100M, ~100-vessel electric-hydrofoil network with JIH Global, phased over 3 years (first 5 vessels in 2026)
precedents.why_it_matters: Demonstrates an all-electric foiling network financed and deployed at scale for a high-end, water-defined destination — directly transferable to a premium charter coast.
